name: dump1090-fa
desc: FlightAware ADS-B Ground Station System for SDRs
why: Turns a cheap SDR dongle into a live map of overhead aircraft by decoding ADS-B squitters broadcast in plain sight.

brief.what_it_is: dump1090-fa is an ADS-B, Mode S, and Mode 3A/3C demodulator and decoder from FlightAware. It takes radio samples from a directly connected software defined radio (SDR) or aircraft data delivered over a network connection, and decodes the aircraft transponder messages. Its output is a live display of nearby aircraft, either in a terminal or as a browser map. It can also feed crowd-sourced flight data to FlightAware when paired with PiAware.
brief.why_it_exists: The README presents it as the successor to dump1090-mutability and as a FlightAware ground station component. It packages local aircraft reception for Debian and Raspbian and supports contributing crowd-sourced tracking data to FlightAware through PiAware.
brief.how_it_works: It demodulates and decodes ADS-B, Mode S, and Mode 3A/3C transponder messages. The README says it uses starch to build several versions of the DSP code and picks the fastest one the hardware supports at runtime, controlled by 'wisdom files' that list implementations in priority order. Default wisdom is compiled in for x86, ARM 32-bit, and ARM 64-bit, and users can generate their own with a benchmark run.

brief.install_notes: You need SDR hardware (RTL-SDR, bladeRF, HackRF, LimeSDR, or a SoapySDR-supported device) or a network feed of aircraft data. The Debian build needs the listed apt packages. Building with limited SDR support is documented for bullseye and buster only, and you can build with no SDR support at all for network-only use. Manual installs require `make`, after which you must place the binaries and set up your own way of starting them. Optionally, generate a wisdom file on an idle system with CPU frequency scaling disabled, copy it to /etc/dump1090-fa/wisdom.local for package installs, and restart dump1090. For manual installs, pass --wisdom /path/to/wisdom.local. The README does not describe a first-run command for viewing aircraft.
brief.standout: It benchmarks its own DSP code at build or install time and selects the fastest implementation the hardware supports, using a wisdom file mechanism. It also serves both sides of the hobbyist-to-network pipeline, a local display and optional crowd-sourced upload through PiAware.
brief.status: Maintained, per the README, which says FlightAware maintains it and names it the successor to dump1090-mutability. The fetched README shows no release or commit date, so I could not confirm recent activity.
brief.caveats: Packaging is aimed at Debian and Raspbian; the README says it should build on other Linux and Unix-like systems. The macOS (Mojave 10.14.6) and FreeBSD (12.1-RELEASE) build notes are marked 'Minimal testing... YMMV'. The example release names (bullseye, buster, stretch) are old, and limited-profile builds are supported only for bullseye and buster. Wisdom generation takes tens of minutes and gives stable results only on an idle system with CPU frequency scaling disabled. The README does not mention a license, and I did not see one in the fetched text. The README gives no usage examples for running the viewer or map.

entry.title: dump1090-fa
entry.tldr: Decodes the transponder messages airplanes broadcast overhead, turning a cheap SDR dongle into a live aircraft display in a terminal or browser map.
entry.deeper_look:
dump1090-fa is an ADS-B, Mode S, and Mode 3A/3C demodulator and decoder from FlightAware. It takes raw radio samples from a software defined radio plugged into your machine, or aircraft data arriving over a network connection, and decodes the transponder messages. The result is a list of nearby aircraft in a terminal, or a map in a browser.

The idea underneath is that aircraft announce who they are and where they are, unencrypted, on a known frequency, and anyone with an antenna can listen. Nothing is hacked here. The tool is a door into how radio samples become bits, how bits become position reports, and how a pile of hobbyist receivers can add up to a global tracking network.

It is the FlightAware ground station component and the successor to dump1090-mutability. Paired with PiAware, it can also send what your antenna hears to FlightAware as crowd-sourced data. You can use it purely locally, too.

There is a neat trick inside. It uses starch to build several versions of the DSP code and picks the fastest one your hardware supports at runtime. Priority lists called wisdom files control the choice, with defaults compiled in for x86, ARM 32-bit, and ARM 64-bit. You can also generate your own with a benchmark run.
entry.install:
brew install dump1090-fa
# Needs an SDR (RTL-SDR, bladeRF, HackRF, LimeSDR, or a SoapySDR device) and an antenna, or a network feed of aircraft data.

entry.whats_unique: It benchmarks its own DSP code and selects the fastest implementation for the hardware via wisdom files. It also covers both ends of the hobby: a local display and optional upload to a crowd-sourced network through PiAware.
entry.caveats: You need SDR hardware or a network feed to see anything, packaging is aimed at Debian and Raspbian, and the README gives no usage examples for the viewer or map.
